name: Warren A. Cowdery
role: Presiding high priest at Freedom and Kirtland clerk
dateNote: He was baptized in 1834 and called to preside at Freedom on 25 November 1834; he recorded the 3 April 1836 visions.
importance: Section 106 calls him to preside over the Church in Freedom, New York, and nearby areas. It also warns him about the vanity of his heart. After moving to Kirtland he worked as an editor and clerk. He wrote the account of the 3 April 1836 temple visions in Joseph Smith’s journal, which became section 110.
connections: He was an older brother of Oliver Cowdery. He became disaffected from Church leaders in 1838.

sources.title: Warren A. Cowdery, Joseph Smith Papers biography

reviewNote: JSP: born 17 Oct. 1788, Wells, Vermont; moved to Freedom 1816; baptized 1834; presiding elder 25 Nov. 1834; moved to Kirtland Feb. 1836; editor of the Messenger and Advocate and clerk; disaffected 1838; died 23 Feb. 1851, Kirtland (date range partly cut off). His role recording section 110 is from that section’s setting. “Warren” alone occurs only in section 106.
